text: What is the primary purpose of HTML forms on a website?
explanation: HTML forms are primarily used to collect various types of user input, which can then be sent to a server for processing.

text: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as an element of an HTML form?
explanation: Standard HTML form elements include labels, checkboxes, and radio buttons. Image sliders are typically custom widgets or require specialized implementation.

text: Which input type allows the user to select only one option from a group?
explanation: Radio buttons are designed for cases where exactly one option must be chosen from a group.

text: What happens when a reset button is clicked in an HTML form?
choices: The form is submitted to the server
The form values are cleared and set to default
explanation: The reset button clears all current user entries in the form and restores elements to their default values.

text: Which combination of information best represents the different types of data that can be collected using HTML forms, as stated in the passage?
choices: Only personal information and login credentials
Personal information, product feedback, surveys, and payment details
Website layout data and server configuration details
Source code and graphical interface settings
explanation: Forms are versatile and can collect personal data, feedback, survey answers, and payment information.

text: Why is KompoZer described as a fast and simple tool for creating HTML forms?
choices: It supports only text-based form creation
It provides a WYSIWYG graphical interface for form design
It directly stores user data in databases
explanation: KompoZer uses a 'What You See Is What You Get' interface, allowing users to design forms visually without writing code.

text: Why does CSS significantly reduce redundancy when styling large HTML documents?
choices: It replaces HTML tags with graphical components
It allows styling rules to be applied globally using selectors
It embeds styles directly into each HTML element
It converts HTML content into visual templates
explanation: CSS selectors allow a single rule to apply to many elements across the entire document, avoiding repeated style definitions.

text: In the CSS rule selector { property : value }, which part determines where the style will be applied?
explanation: The selector targets specific HTML elements to which the defined styles will be applied.

text: Which statement best explains the conceptual difference between HTML and CSS as described in the passage?
choices: HTML controls layout while CSS controls data
HTML defines content, while CSS defines presentation
CSS stores content and HTML formats it
Both HTML and CSS perform the same role
explanation: HTML is for the structure and content of the page, while CSS handles the visual style and presentation.

text:
Why is using CSS preferred over repeatedly applying the tag to multiple

elements?
choices: CSS allows centralized styling and easier maintenance
CSS automatically converts tags into bold
explanation: CSS allows global styling changes from one location, making it much easier to maintain than individual formatting tags.

text: Which statement best explains how CSS helps prevent accidental data modification in a website?
choices: By embedding style rules directly inside HTML tags
By separating layout and formatting from the logical structure
By converting HTML content into dynamic scripts
explanation: Separating style from structure ensures that changes to the appearance don't accidentally alter the underlying data or logic.

text: What limitation of early HTML led to the development of JavaScript?
choices: HTML could not support CSS styling
HTML pages were static after being rendered by the browser
HTML did not support form elements
HTML could not load external resources
explanation: Standard HTML pages are static; JavaScript was created to add interactivity and dynamic behavior after the page is loaded.

text: In client-side form validation using JavaScript, which condition is checked before data is sent to the server?
choices: Whether required fields are empty or incorrectly formatted
Logical structure of the HTML document
explanation: JavaScript validates that the user has filled out required fields and that the data format (like email) is correct before submission.

text: Which of the following best describes a JavaScript function as defined in the passage?
choices: A variable that stores user input
A reusable block of code that performs a specific task
A built-in object used to control the browser
A conditional statement that validates data
explanation: A function is a discrete, reusable block of code designed to perform a particular action or calculation.

text: What is the primary purpose of the built-in JavaScript function alert()?
choices: To return a value from a function
To display text in an alert box
To set focus on an HTML element
explanation: The alert() function is used to pop up a message box to show information or warnings to the user.

text: What happens when a return statement is executed inside a JavaScript function?
choices: The function pauses and resumes later
The function stops executing and sends back a value
The function continues execution after returning a value
The function displays an alert message
explanation: Executing 'return' immediately stops function execution and passes the specified value back to the caller.

text: In the given example, when is the function validateForm() executed?
choices: When the submit button is clicked
When the alert box is displayed
explanation: Form validation functions are usually triggered by high-level events like clicking the 'Submit' button.

text: Which statement correctly explains how a JavaScript function can be invoked?
choices: Only from the head section of HTML
Automatically without any event or call
By an event or by calling it inside the source code
explanation: Functions can be executed in response to user actions (events) or directly called by other parts of the script.

text: What causes a JavaScript event to occur according to the passage?
choices: An action performed by the user
Definition of a variable in the script
explanation: Events are typically triggered by user interactions like clicks, keypresses, or window resizing.

text: Which of the following conditions will cause isNaN(value) to return true according to the passage?
choices: When value contains exactly six numeric digits
When value is a numeric string like "123"
When value represents non-numeric data such as "hello"
When value is an empty string only
explanation: The isNaN() function checks if a value is 'Not-a-Number'. It returns true for non-numeric data.

text: Which statement correctly describes the behavior of static members in a class?
choices: They are created separately for each object of the class
They are allocated memory once per class and shared by all objects
They can be accessed only through instance objects
They belong only to constructors and not to the class
explanation: Static members belong to the class itself, not to individual instances, and are shared by all objects of that class.

text: What does publishing a website mean according to the passage?
choices: Designing web pages using an IDE
Transferring website files to a web server for user access
Creating user accounts on the Internet
Buying software licenses for web development
explanation: Publishing involves uploading the website's files to a server so it can be accessed by the public via the internet.

text: Which of the following is mentioned as a free open-source web development IDE?
explanation: While others are popular, Blue Griffon is specifically highlighted in some curricula as a free open-source visual editor.

text: According to the passage, what was the primary purpose of earlier websites?
choices: Disseminating information about products or organizations
explanation: Early websites were primarily informational, used by organizations to share details about themselves or their products.

text: Which activity is explicitly identified as part of E-commerce business operations?
choices: Trading stocks and providing customer service
explanation: E-commerce includes various business activities like online trading, stock transactions, and digital customer support.

text: Which statement best explains how E-commerce benefits businesses and consumers?
choices: It limits business operations to local markets
It increases costs but improves product quality
It overcomes time and distance barriers and improves delivery speed
It reduces product variety available to consumers
explanation: E-commerce allows 24/7 access regardless of location, eliminating physical proximity requirements for buying and selling.

text: What is the primary purpose of online billing as described in the passage?
choices: To allow companies to send bills and receive payments electronically
explanation: Online billing systems replace paper bills with electronic ones, facilitating faster and more efficient payment collection.

text: Which of the following is an example of Information Services?
choices: Sending examination results and notices through websites
explanation: Information services involve the dissemination of data, such as educational results or public notices, via websites.

text: Why are certain products like perishable food items difficult to sell through E-commerce?
choices: Customers cannot touch or examine them before purchase
explanation: Some products require physical inspection or have short lifespans, making them less suitable for the indirect nature of online sales.

text: Which feature differentiates E-commerce from traditional commerce according to the passage?
choices: Requires physical store layout and merchandising
Uses electronic advertising and online product catalogues
explanation: E-commerce relies on digital marketing and online catalogs rather than physical displays and traditional advertising.

text: Which limitation of E-commerce is related to fear of misuse of personal and financial data?
explanation: Privacy concerns stem from the risk that sensitive personal or financial information might be stolen or misused.

text: In which E-commerce business model do consumers directly sell products to other consumers?
explanation: C2C models involve individual consumers transacting with each other, often through online facilitators or marketplaces.

text: Which E-commerce model allows consumers to decide the price they are willing to pay, and businesses bid accordingly?
explanation: In Consumer-to-Business (C2B), consumers set conditions or prices, and businesses compete to fulfill them.

text: Which of the following is a limitation of M-commerce related to device hardware?
explanation: Mobile devices naturally have less processing power and storage compared to desktop computers, which can limit complex applications.

text: Why is displaying videos sometimes difficult in M-commerce?
choices: Due to limited screen size and bandwidth
Due to absence of software support
Due to high cost of mobile devices
explanation: Small screens and potentially unstable mobile networks make high-quality video streaming more challenging on mobile devices.

text: Which service uses the mobile user’s location to provide nearby store details?
explanation: Location and search services use GPS or cell data to offer local information, such as finding a nearby restaurant or shop.

text: What is L-commerce primarily based on?
explanation: L-commerce (Location-based commerce) uses the geographic position of a mobile user to provide relevant services or offers.

text: Which security principle ensures that data is not altered during transmission?
explanation: Integrity ensures that information remains accurate and unchanged while being sent over a network.

text: Which Internet security threat involves pretending to be a legitimate website?
explanation: Spoofing is an attack where an untrusted source masquerades as a known, trusted source to gain access or steal data.

text: What is the main purpose of cryptography in E-commerce?
explanation: Cryptography uses complex algorithms to encrypt sensitive data, ensuring only authorized parties can read it.

text: Which technique hides information inside images, audio, or text files?
explanation: Steganography is the practice of concealing a file, message, image, or video within another file.

text: How does a charge card differ from a credit card?
choices: It has a lower interest rate
It does not have a spending limit
explanation: Typically, charge cards do not have a pre-set spending limit but require the full balance to be paid every month.

text: Which payment system transfers money electronically between bank accounts?
explanation: EFT is the general term for transferring money from one bank account to another using electronic systems.

text: In object-oriented methodology, what fundamentally distinguishes one object from another object of the same class?
choices: The methods defined in the class
The values of attributes representing its state
explanation: While they share same methods, objects are distinguished by the specific data (state) they hold in their attributes.

text: Which relationship represents an exclusive “has-a” association where the contained object cannot exist independently?
explanation: Composition is a strong 'has-a' relationship where the life of the child object is managed by the parent object.

text: How does encapsulation primarily protect data in object-oriented programming?
choices: By exposing all variables as public
By restricting direct access and allowing controlled interaction through methods
explanation: Encapsulation bundles data and methods together and controls access to the data, hiding the internal implementation.

text: Which statement best differentiates data abstraction from encapsulation?
choices: Abstraction hides data; encapsulation hides behavior
Encapsulation hides implementation details; abstraction hides complexity of usage
Encapsulation focuses on interfaces; abstraction focuses on security
explanation: Encapsulation is about shielding the internal workings, while abstraction is about showing only relevant features to the outside world.

text: In method invocation, how does an object determine which version of a method with the same name should be executed?
choices: By the return type of the method
By the object that invokes the method
explanation: In dynamic polymorphism, the specific method to execute is determined at runtime based on the actual object type calling it.

text: Which feature of object-oriented programming allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists?
explanation: Method overloading is a form of compile-time polymorphism where methods share the same name but have different signatures.

text: Operator overloading contributes to polymorphism because it:
choices: Allows operators to have different meanings for different object types
Restricts operator usage to numeric data
explanation: It allows standard operators like '+' or '*' to work in specialized ways for user-defined classes.

text: Why is a class described as a “blueprint” in object-oriented programming?
choices: It represents common attributes and behaviors shared by multiple objects
explanation: A class provides the template or structure from which individual objects (instances) are created.

text: Which statement best explains why a class variable is declared using the static keyword?
choices: To allocate memory every time an object is created
To ensure the variable belongs to an object instance
To allocate memory once per class and share it among all objects
To restrict access to subclasses only
explanation: Static (class) variables are shared by all instances of a class; only one copy of the variable exists.

text: What happens if a class defines no constructor explicitly?
choices: The compiler inserts a parameterized constructor
A default no-argument constructor is automatically provided
explanation: If no constructor is provided, the Java compiler automatically adds a public, no-argument default constructor.

text: Which of the following variables is not initialized with a default value in Java?
explanation: Local variables (defined inside methods) must be explicitly initialized before use; they don't get default values.

text: In Java, which statement about reference variables is TRUE?
choices: They store the address of an object in heap memory
explanation: Reference variables do not contain the object itself; they contain a memory address pointing to where the object is stored.

text: Constructors differ from normal methods because they:
choices: Must have the same name as the class and no return type
Are executed only once per class
explanation: Constructors have no return type and must match the class name exactly. They are called during object instantiation.

text: Which concept allows methods with the same name but different parameter lists in Java?
explanation: Method overloading allows a class to have multiple methods with the same name as long as their parameters differ.

text: In inheritance, which relationship is correctly described?
choices: Subclass is a subset of superclass
explanation: Inheritance defines an 'is-a' relationship (e.g., a Dog *is a*n Animal), where the subclass extends the superclass.

text: Which members of a superclass are not inherited by a subclass?
explanation: While subclasses can call superclass constructors using 'super()', they do not technically inherit them.

text: Why are getter and setter methods preferred over public variables?
choices: They support data encapsulation and controlled access
They eliminate the need for constructors
explanation: Accessor and mutator methods allow a class to control how its internal data is accessed or modified, protecting its integrity.

text: What is the primary purpose of the new keyword in Java?
choices: Allocating memory for an object and returning its reference
explanation: The 'new' operator allocates memory on the heap for a new object and calls the appropriate constructor.

text: Which access modifier provides the widest visibility in Java?
explanation: The 'public' modifier allows the element to be accessed from any other class or package in the application.

text: Which access level allows visibility only within the same package and subclasses?
explanation: The 'protected' modifier makes a member accessible within its own package and by subclasses in other packages.

text: When an object is no longer referenced, how is its memory reclaimed in Java?
explanation: Java has automatic memory management; the Garbage Collector identifies and deletes objects that are no longer in use.

text: Which of the following correctly describes instance variables?
choices: Created when an object is instantiated and unique per object
explanation: Instance variables belong to a specific object; each instance gets its own copy of these variables.

text: Which statement about polymorphism in Java is CORRECT?
choices: It allows one method name to perform different tasks
explanation: Polymorphism (meaning 'many forms') allows the same method to behave differently depending on the object it acts upon.

text: In Java, an array is best described as:
choices: A collection of variables of different data types
A collection of homogeneous data elements stored contiguously
A collection of objects stored randomly in memory
A dynamic data structure like a list
explanation: An array is a fixed-size container that holds elements of the same type in adjacent memory locations.

text: Which of the following correctly declares a 1-D integer array in Java?
explanation: Java supports 'type variable[]' or 'type[] variable' syntax for array declarations.

text: What is the default initial value of elements in an int array in Java?
explanation: When an integer array is initialized, Java automatically sets all its elements to zero.

text: Which statement about array index in Java is correct?
explanation: Java arrays are zero-indexed; the first element is at index 0 and the last is at index (length - 1).

text: In Java, array name represents:
choices: A reference variable to memory location
explanation: The array identifier is a reference variable that points to the start of the array's memory on the heap.

text: Which class provides utility methods like sort() and fill() for arrays?
explanation: The java.util.Arrays class contains various static methods for manipulating arrays (such as sorting and searching).

text: Which method is used to get the length of a String in Java?
explanation: In Java, String objects have a length() method, whereas arrays have a length property.

text: Which of the following correctly compares the content of two strings?
explanation: The equals() method checks if two String objects contain the same sequence of characters.

text: What does compareTo() method return when two strings are equal?
explanation: The compareTo() method returns zero if the two strings are lexicographically equal.

text: Which String method converts all characters to lowercase?
explanation: toLowerCase() returns a new string with all capital letters converted to their lowercase equivalents.

text: Which constructor creates a String object using a character array?
explanation: String has a constructor that accepts an array of characters and uses them to build the string content.

text: When two String objects are created using the same string literal, they:
choices: Refer to the same memory location
explanation: Java uses a 'String Pool'; literals with identical content point to the same shared object in memory to save space.

text: Which Date class method returns milliseconds elapsed since 1 Jan 1970?
explanation: The getTime() method returns the number of milliseconds since the epoch (January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 GMT).

text: Which Calendar constant represents hour in 24-hour format?
explanation: HOUR_OF_DAY is used for a 24-hour clock (0-23), while HOUR is for a 12-hour clock (0-11).

text: In Calendar class, month value for January is:
explanation: Java's Calendar API uses 0 for January, 1 for February, and so on up to 11 for December.

text: Which method sets date and time using milliseconds in Date class?
explanation: The setTime(long time) method updates a Date object to represent a specific point in time in milliseconds since the epoch.

text: Which of the following is NOT true about Java arrays?
choices: Arrays store elements in contiguous memory
Declaring an array allocates memory automatically
Array elements are initialized with default values
explanation: Declaring an array variable does not allocate memory for the elements; you must use 'new' to allocate that space.

text: Skype primarily allows users to communicate using which combination of services?
explanation: Skype is a VoIP service that supports instant messaging, voice calls, and video conferencing.

text: Calls made between Skype users are:
explanation: Voice and video calls between two Skype accounts are generally free over the internet.

text: Which of the following best describes the source code availability of Skype?
choices: Proprietary and not available for modification
explanation: Skype is a proprietary software owned by Microsoft; its source code is not publicly available.

text: Google Maps collects map data using all of the following EXCEPT:
explanation: Google Maps uses sophisticated data sources like satellites and Street View cars, rather than just manual drawings.

text: On mobile phones, Google Maps can determine a user’s location most accurately using:
explanation: Global Positioning System (GPS) provides the most precise coordinate data for mobile device location.

text: The default view shown when Google Maps is opened is:
explanation: The standard 'Map view' is the default interface showing roads, borders, and place names.

text: Which compressed file format is most commonly used on Linux systems for distributing software bundles?
explanation: The 'tarball' format (.tar.gz) is the standard for packaging and compressing files in the Linux ecosystem.

text: Archive Manager in Linux is mainly used for:
choices: Creating, extracting, and managing archive files
explanation: The Archive Manager (like File Roller) handles compressed files like ZIP, TAR, and GZ.

text: VLC Media Player is popular mainly because of its:
explanation: VLC is highly regarded for being free, open-source, and able to play almost any media format without extra codecs.

text: The primary goal of data compression is to:
choices: Reduce memory and disk space usage
explanation: Compression reduces the physical size of a file, saving storage space and making transfers faster.

text: HTML stands for:
explanation: HTML is the standard language used to create the structure and content of web pages.

text: HTTP stands for:
explanation: HTTP is the foundational protocol used by the World Wide Web for data communication.

text: UML stands for:
explanation: UML is a standardized modeling language used to visualize the design of a software system.

text: API stands for:
explanation: An API is a set of rules and protocols that allows different software applications to communicate with each other.

text: PHP stands for:
explanation: While originally meaning 'Personal Home Page', PHP's modern recursive backronym is 'PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor'.

text: JVM stands for:
explanation: The JVM is the engine that provides the runtime environment to drive Java code (bytecode).

text: IRCTC stands for:
choices: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation
Indian Rail Coach and Travel Company
Indian Railway Cargo and Transport Corporation
Indian Rail Catering and Ticket Corporation
explanation: IRCTC is a subsidiary of the Indian Railways that handles the online ticketing, catering, and tourism operations.
